rows: Value can be assigned only once (constant).
Cannot be overridden by a subclass.

items: Must be initialized when declared or in a constructor.
Its value cannot be changed once assigned.
When a method is marked as final, it cannot be overridden in any subclass.
A final class cannot be extended.
Ensures that the implementation of the class cannot be altered by subclassing.

sections.heading: ❌ Attempt to extend a final class:

content.code:
class HomeLoan extends Loan {  // ❌ Error: cannot inherit from final class
}

items: A final variable behaves like a constant.
A final method guarantees that behavior won't change in subclasses.
A final class provides security and stability by preventing inheritance.
Static methods cannot be overridden, even if not declared as final (they belong to the class, not instances).

codeBlocks.code:
class HomeLoan extends Loan {  // ❌ Error: cannot inherit from final class
}
